observations: The page number «57» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. At the foot, the signature line of the printed sheet: «D. K. D. Vidensk. Selsk. Skr., 7. Række, hist. og filos. Afd. III. 1.» on the left and the sheet number «8» on the right; recorded here, not transcribed as a line. L01-L07 continue the first case of p. 56 (JP2 0088, L33-L35).
L03 and L06: the two divisions are printed as built-up fractions, «5° 45½′» and «224° 34½′» over «57′», written {fr:NUMERATOR|DENOMINATOR}; «45½′», «34½′» with the raised 1 and the lowered 2.

L01-L07. Checked: the first station of Saturn, 115° 10′, less its anomaly, 109° 24½′ (pp. 55-56, JP2 0087-0088), is 5° 45½′, and 345½′ : 57′ = 6.06, about 6 days; the anomaly plus the first station, 109° 24½′ + 115° 10′ = 224° 34½′, the arc from the second station, 244° 50′, through 360° to the anomaly (note 1: 360° − 244° 50′ + 109° 24½′ = 224° 34½′), and 13474½′ : 57′ = 236.4, 236 days; 236 + 6 = 242. The daily motion of 57′ is that of note 2 of p. 56 (JP2 0088), 57′ 8″, in whole minutes.

A figure stands at the right of L17-L25, which are set in a narrower measure at its left; it is not reproduced. The circle of the epicycle about H, with A at the left end and P at the right end of a horizontal line through H, which runs on to E far to the right; on the circle K at the upper left, C at the upper right, B at the lower right, G at the lower left and D at the bottom, marked with a short stroke; the lines E C K, E B G and the tangent E D; F on the chord G B, joined to H by a line perpendicular to the chord, so that F is its middle; a small arrow at A pointing down and one between P and C pointing up, the direction of the planet on the epicycle. The letters are italic: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, K, P.

L16-L29: the stations after Apollonius, as Ptolemy gives them (Almagest XII, 1): the planet is stationary at B, where half the chord, F B, is to B E as the speed of the centre of the epicycle to that of the planet on the epicycle; retrograde on the arc B C nearest the earth, direct on the arc C A B. Checked: with the anomaly counted from A in the direction of the arrows, A G B P C K, the station B has an anomaly less than 180° and C its complement to 360°, as on p. 55 (JP2 0087, L18-L22).

L26 and L27: «FB ∶ BE», the colon of the ratio with a space on either side (16-18 px), written ∶ (U+2236). N08: «267– 302», a short dash (13 px), lighter than the print, with a space after it, where «450—494» in the same line has the long dash set close; transcribed as printed, as «151– 152» on p. XI (JP2 0014, N07). N01: «(360° — Stat. II.)», the minus sign printed as a long dash with a space on either side.

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Ptol.», «Batt.», «Kh.», «Nallinos», «Plato von Tivoli», «Nallino», «Heiberg», «Manitius»; italics: the letters of the figure, «2. Fall», «Anomal. aeq.» (L08; upright in L02, L05, L09, L12), «grösser», «Deferens», «Centrum» (L31-L32), «aequat.», the Latin of N03. L03: «stationnär», as on p. 55.
The colons and semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (7-16 px measured; «ab ;» in N05, 7 px).
